title: Open project and handle invalid paths
positive: Enter the disposable project directory in Project path and click Open project; repeat using its wrangler.json path.
positive_expected: Status confirms the project opened and its asset selector reflects the project for both path forms.
negative: Enter a nonexistent directory and click Open project.
negative_expected: A visible diagnostic identifies the problem; no unrelated project is opened or changed.
setup: Create the disposable project as described in the guide. Related reported bug: #95.

title: Edit, save and reload a project asset
positive: Open a writable project, select a valid editable JSON asset, change a harmless value, click Save, reopen the project and select the asset again.
positive_expected: The saved value persists and the asset remains valid.
negative: Make the JSON syntactically invalid and click Save.
negative_expected: A diagnostic is shown and the last valid disk file remains intact.
setup: Use a disposable project with an existing valid asset; retain a copy for comparison.

title: Protect drafts and resolve external edits
positive: Edit an asset in the UI; change the same asset externally; use the conflict view and choose Use disk, then repeat choosing Use draft and Save.
positive_expected: The first decision loads the disk version; the second preserves the draft until explicitly saved.
negative: With an unsaved draft, attempt to select another asset or open another project.
negative_expected: The switch is refused with a clear status and the draft is preserved.
setup: Use two distinct valid assets and a disposable project; wait for file watcher refresh.

title: Request lifecycle and persistence
positive: Open a writable project, click New, name a request, set GET and http://127.0.0.1:5057/echo, Save, Close, then select it in Saved project request.
positive_expected: The saved request reopens with its name, method and URL intact.
negative: Attempt to save a request without an open writable project.
negative_expected: A clear diagnostic is shown and no project asset is written.
setup: Start the local fixture and use the disposable project.

title: Send HTTP methods, headers, query and body
positive: Set POST /echo; enter repeated query parameters and headers, select a text body with a distinctive value and click Send. Inspect response body and headers.
positive_expected: The echo response reflects POST and the entered query, headers and body; response metadata is visible.
negative: Enter a malformed header line and send.
negative_expected: Input is rejected with a diagnostic and no successful response is presented for that request.
setup: Use http://127.0.0.1:5057/echo; use only synthetic values.

title: Body formats and uploads
positive: Select raw body mode, enter {"value":1}, click Format body and send to /echo; repeat using file body mode with valid.json as upload path.
positive_expected: Valid JSON formats in raw mode and the fixture receives the intended JSON or file bytes respectively.
negative: Enter malformed JSON and format; then select file mode with a nonexistent file and send.
negative_expected: Each invalid input produces a visible error; no unrelated file is sent.
setup: Start the fixture; use docs/ui-testing/data/valid.json as the local file.

title: HTTP cancellation and response views
positive: Send GET /delay and click Cancel before ten seconds; then send GET /echo and inspect body, headers, cookies, view modes and local artifact path.
positive_expected: Cancellation is reported promptly, the UI remains usable, and the following request displays its own response and artifact.
negative: Send an invalid or unreachable URL.
negative_expected: A clear transport or URL error is shown; stale successful output is not represented as the new response.
setup: Start the fixture on 127.0.0.1:5057.

title: Redirects and transport security
positive: Send GET /redirect with Follow redirects enabled, then disabled.
positive_expected: Enabled follows to /echo; disabled shows the redirect response.
negative: Enter a URL containing embedded credentials or an invalid scheme and send.
negative_expected: The unsafe or invalid URL is rejected visibly and credentials are not exposed.
setup: Use the local fixture; do not use real credentials.

title: Authentication and variable inspection
positive: Configure a synthetic Basic or bearer credential, send to /echo, and inspect the received header; inspect a defined project/environment variable.
positive_expected: The intended auth is applied and variable inspection shows the resolved non-secret value without exposing secret values.
negative: Reference an undefined variable or supply incomplete authentication and send.
negative_expected: The UI reports the problem without sending an unintended credential or leaking a secret.
setup: Use test-only credentials and a disposable project/environment; sanitize any evidence.

title: Dataset preview and import
positive: Open a writable project, select valid.csv, CSV and UTF-8, enter a dataset name, prepare preview, then accept import.
positive_expected: Two rows with the original unique case IDs appear in preview and the dataset is published only after acceptance.
negative: Select duplicate-ids.csv and prepare preview.
negative_expected: Duplicate case IDs are diagnosed and no dataset is published.
setup: Use docs/ui-testing/data and the disposable project.

title: Dataset formats, conversion and missing IDs
positive: Import missing-ids.csv with explicit case-ID addition enabled; prepare and accept. Repeat with valid.json as JSON.
positive_expected: Preview includes unique generated IDs and the accepted rows match preview; JSON rows retain their IDs.
negative: Prepare missing-ids.csv with case-ID addition disabled, then prepare malformed.json as JSON.
negative_expected: Both inputs produce clear validation errors and neither creates a dataset.
setup: Use an isolated project and docs/ui-testing/data.

title: Dataset stale preview and cancellation
positive: Prepare valid.csv; alter the source file on disk without changing UI settings, then accept.
positive_expected: Accepted rows match the prepared preview, not the later source edit.
negative: Prepare again, change an import setting, then click Accept import; also cancel an active preparation.
negative_expected: A stale preview cannot be accepted; cancellation does not publish a dataset.
setup: Work on a disposable copy of valid.csv. Use a sufficiently large local file for cancellation if necessary.

title: Import preview and publish
positive: Open a writable project, enter a supported cURL command for GET http://127.0.0.1:5057/echo, choose its format, preview and publish.
positive_expected: The preview describes the imported request, and explicit publish creates the project asset without executing it.
negative: Preview malformed source or attempt publish without a valid preview.
negative_expected: An actionable diagnostic appears or publish remains unavailable; no asset is created and no command runs.
setup: Use a disposable project; check the fixture receives no request during preview/publish.

title: GraphQL formatting and execution
positive: Paste sample.graphql, click Format, enter http://127.0.0.1:5061/graphql and execute; inspect response.
positive_expected: Valid query formatting preserves meaning and the fixture returns data.health = ready.
negative: Enter malformed GraphQL or malformed variables JSON and format or execute.
negative_expected: The error is visible, the app stays open, and no false success is shown.
setup: Start docs/ui-testing/protocol_fixture.py on port 5061; use data/sample.graphql.

title: gRPC proto parse and simulated call
positive: Paste sample.proto, click Parse Proto, enter the matching method and valid JSON payload, then click Simulate Call.
positive_expected: The service/method parses and the transcript clearly shows the simulated result.
negative: Enter malformed proto or invalid payload JSON and invoke the corresponding action.
negative_expected: The UI shows an error without crashing or claiming a successful call.
setup: Use sample.proto; this control is a simulation, not proof of network gRPC.

title: WebSocket and SSE connection lifecycle
positive: Connect to ws://127.0.0.1:5061/ws, send hello, inspect transcript and disconnect; connect to http://127.0.0.1:5061/events and observe the event.
positive_expected: The transcript shows the echoed WebSocket message and fixture-ready SSE event; disconnect ends the session.
negative: Connect to an invalid or unavailable endpoint and try sending after disconnect.
negative_expected: Failure is visible, no message is claimed delivered, and the UI remains responsive.
setup: Start docs/ui-testing/protocol_fixture.py on port 5061.

title: Mock rules, matching and logs
positive: Start the local mock on loopback, add a GET rule for /qa with status 200 and a distinctive JSON body, send a local request to it, then Refresh Logs and Reset State.
positive_expected: The rule returns its configured response, the request appears in logs, and reset clears state as indicated.
negative: Try to start on an occupied port and add a rule with invalid input.
negative_expected: Errors are visible; no second listener or invalid rule is silently installed.
setup: Choose a free loopback port and occupy a different local port for the negative variant.

title: Mock faults and external bind guard
positive: Create a delayed-response or HTTP-error rule and send a matching local request.
positive_expected: The configured fault is observable and logged.
negative: Attempt a non-loopback bind without selecting Allow external binding.
negative_expected: The listener refuses external binding with a visible diagnostic.
setup: Use only an isolated local test environment; stop the listener after the case.

title: Webhook listener capture
positive: Start the webhook listener with a test path prefix, send a local POST with a synthetic payload, then Refresh Events and stop the listener.
positive_expected: The event and count appear and the listener stops.
negative: Send to a nonmatching path or after stopping the listener.
negative_expected: It is not recorded as a matching live event; any connection failure is reported by the sender.
setup: Use only loopback and synthetic data; determine the displayed listener URL before sending.

title: Load test run, thresholds and cancellation
positive: Target local /echo with one virtual user, short duration, a permissive threshold and explicit target confirmation; click Start Test and inspect metrics. Repeat and cancel while running.
positive_expected: The completed report contains request and percentile metrics; cancellation is visible and returns control.
negative: Clear explicit confirmation and click Start Test; also try an invalid target URL.
negative_expected: The test is refused with a diagnostic and no traffic is sent.
setup: Start the local fixture. Never use a public endpoint for load tests.

title: Synthetic dataset browsing
positive: Open the tab and scroll through the 100,000 synthetic rows, including near the end.
positive_expected: Rows display with case ID, email and status; scrolling remains responsive.
negative: Attempt to edit a cell or add a row.
negative_expected: The read-only fixture does not accept or persist an edit.
setup: Desktop application running.

title: Grid editing, filter and undo
positive: Insert a row, edit email and status, duplicate a case, filter for the email, clear filter, undo and redo an edit.
positive_expected: Changes, filtered results and undo/redo reflect the selected operations; duplicate case identity remains unique.
negative: Apply a filter with no match and attempt an operation requiring a selection with no row selected.
negative_expected: No unrelated row changes; empty results or an actionable status is shown.
setup: Use a fresh desktop session and synthetic values.

title: Clipboard, safe export and external results
positive: Copy valid.csv content to clipboard, click Paste clipboard, then export CSV with spreadsheet-safe export enabled; attach synthetic external results.
positive_expected: Rows are previewed/imported as supported, exported data is readable, and attached results are identified as external.
negative: Paste malformed data or a cURL command containing a harmless local URL; include a cell beginning =1+1 in an export.
negative_expected: Malformed content is diagnosed; cURL is not executed; spreadsheet-safe export neutralizes the formula cell.
setup: Use a disposable export location and inspect output as plain text; do not open unsafe data in a spreadsheet.

title: Git initialize, status and branches
positive: Set an empty disposable repository path, Initialize, Refresh, create a branch and switch to it; inspect status and history.
positive_expected: Repository and branch operations are reflected in the UI and existing data outside the repository is untouched.
negative: Set an invalid Git executable or invalid repository path and refresh.
negative_expected: The UI reports the Git/path error without crashing or changing another repository.
setup: Use an empty temporary directory and installed Git; create an initial commit if branch operations require it.

title: Git review and commit selected assets
positive: Change one disposable project asset, enter its repository-relative path and commit message, review selected files, inspect the diff, then commit reviewed files.
positive_expected: The displayed diff matches the selected change and the commit includes only reviewed files.
negative: Change a selected file after review or leave the commit message invalid, then attempt commit.
negative_expected: Stale or invalid review is rejected and no unintended commit is made.
setup: Use a disposable Git repository with a baseline commit and configured local identity.

title: Git conflicts and resolution
positive: Create a conflict in a disposable project asset, Find conflicts, Load versions, review local or incoming version and mark the reviewed path resolved.
positive_expected: Base/local/incoming and final diff are visible and only the reviewed resolution is staged.
negative: Attempt to resolve without reviewing, or use an invalid save-both path.
negative_expected: Resolution is refused and conflict versions remain recoverable.
setup: Create two divergent local branches editing the same project asset and merge to produce a conflict.

title: Git remotes and integration failures
positive: Use a disposable local bare repository as remote; add/select it, fetch, push a test branch and inspect history.
positive_expected: Remote and branch state update as requested without exposing credentials.
negative: Fetch an unreachable remote or fast-forward a divergent branch.
negative_expected: The error is visible and local work is not silently overwritten.
setup: Create a local bare repository and working clone; use no production repository or credentials.

title: Keyboard, accessibility and theme traversal
positive: Navigate every top-level tab by keyboard, change font family and size, use access keys and Ctrl+Enter on a local request, and inspect focus at normal and high-contrast settings.
positive_expected: All tabs render, controls are reachable with visible focus, font settings affect editors and the shortcut sends the request.
negative: Navigate with no project open and attempt unavailable actions; check for clipped controls or unlabeled focus targets.
negative_expected: Unavailable actions are disabled or explain their prerequisites; focus remains visible and no crash occurs.
setup: Use Windows 11 x64; Narrator speech observation remains separately tracked in #58.

title: Project read-only ownership and recovery
setup: Use a disposable project and two application instances.
positive: Open the same project in both instances; inspect editability, then close the owner and reopen in the second instance.
positive_expected: Only the writer can save; the other instance reports read-only and can later acquire ownership.
negative: Keep a dirty draft, close or interrupt the application and reopen the project.
negative_expected: Recovery or a clear diagnostic preserves the draft; it is not silently applied over disk.

title: Project watcher and disk protection
setup: Open two distinct valid project assets in a disposable project.
positive: Without a dirty draft, edit the selected asset externally and wait for refresh.
positive_expected: The disk and editor views reflect the external version.
negative: Delete or corrupt the selected asset externally while a draft exists.
negative_expected: The UI warns or blocks unsafe save and preserves recoverable content.

title: HTTP method matrix
setup: Start the HTTP fixture at 127.0.0.1:5057.
positive: Send GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and OPTIONS to /echo, then HEAD to /echo.
positive_expected: The fixture reports the chosen method for supported methods; HEAD does not display a response body.
negative: Send to an unavailable port and an unsupported URL scheme.
negative_expected: A transport or validation diagnostic is shown and the app stays responsive.

title: HTTP raw, none and form body modes
setup: Start the HTTP fixture; use /echo.
positive: For POST select each of raw, none, urlencoded and form-data. Send raw {"value":1}, then name=alice and role=qa for the form modes.
positive_expected: Echoed body and Content-Type correspond to each selected mode; none sends no body.
negative: Supply malformed form input or a missing file in file mode and send.
negative_expected: The UI reports the input or file error and does not claim a successful send.

title: HTTP authentication mode matrix
setup: Use local /echo and test-only values user=qa and secret=synthetic-token.
positive: Exercise none, basic, bearer and apiKey, inspecting the echo request headers.
positive_expected: Each mode produces its intended synthetic auth or none; no other mode remains unintentionally active.
negative: Select oauth2, windows and certificate without their prerequisites and try to send.
negative_expected: Unsupported or incomplete configuration is reported; no credential is silently invented or exposed.

title: HTTP variable scope and substitution
setup: Import postman-environment.json into a disposable project; use local /echo.
positive: Select UI QA environment, inspect variables, and send a URL containing {{baseUrl}}/echo.
positive_expected: The resolved value and its scope are displayed and the local fixture receives the request; secret values stay redacted in inspection.
negative: Reference a missing variable and a cyclic pair in a disposable environment.
negative_expected: A diagnostic identifies unresolved or cyclic expansion and no unsafe target is contacted.

title: HTTP response formatting and large data
setup: Start the HTTP fixture.
positive: Send GET /echo, switch Pretty and Raw, then send /large and inspect local artifact.
positive_expected: Pretty and Raw preserve the response content; large output remains usable and its local artifact is accessible.
negative: Attempt to edit response body, headers, cookies or artifact path.
negative_expected: Read-only output does not accept edits or alter saved response bytes.

title: HTTP TLS and redirect security
setup: Use a disposable local HTTPS endpoint with a self-signed certificate and a second local origin; record endpoint setup.
positive: Send with TLS validation enabled and then explicitly enable Ignore TLS errors; test a cross-origin redirect carrying a synthetic Authorization header.
positive_expected: Validation rejects the untrusted certificate by default; explicit override permits the local request and cross-origin redirect strips authorization.
negative: Disable the override again and retry; never use real credentials.
negative_expected: The untrusted certificate is rejected and the test token is not sent to the redirected origin.

title: Dataset format and encoding matrix
setup: Use valid.csv, valid.tsv, valid.json and valid.jsonl plus generated encoding variants from the guide.
positive: Prepare and accept each CSV, TSV, JSON array and JSONL input; repeat CSV with UTF-8, UTF-16 LE and Windows-1252.
positive_expected: Two correct rows and stable case IDs appear for every matching format/encoding.
negative: Choose a deliberately incompatible format or encoding for a non-ASCII file.
negative_expected: The import reports an error or visibly incorrect preview for rejection; no incorrect data is accepted.

title: Dataset mappings and typed conversion
setup: Use conversions.csv in a writable disposable project.
positive: Set mappings to the conversion-mappings.json contents; prepare and accept.
positive_expected: Preview and saved rows contain decimal, boolean and ISO date values, and empty is null as specified.
negative: Change the numeric or date input to an invalid value and prepare.
negative_expected: A conversion diagnostic is shown and no dataset is published.

title: Dataset delimiter culture and quoting
setup: Use quoted.csv and semicolon.csv in data.
positive: Prepare quoted.csv with comma, then semicolon.csv with semicolon and culture de-DE using the supplied decimal mapping.
positive_expected: Quoted commas/newlines are retained as fields and 12,50 converts to decimal 12.50.
negative: Set a multi-character delimiter or an invalid culture and prepare.
negative_expected: The UI reports invalid settings without modifying project assets.

title: Dataset browse and cancellation
setup: Use a disposable writable project and valid.csv; generate the large file as described in the guide.
positive: Use Browse to choose valid.csv and prepare. Cancel the file chooser in a separate attempt.
positive_expected: The chosen path is populated and prepared; cancelling the chooser does not replace the current path.
negative: Cancel preparation and cancel acceptance while processing the large file.
negative_expected: Cancellation is reported; inspect project state before retrying and no earlier dataset is overwritten.

title: Dataset preview bounds and repeat acceptance
setup: Generate the 1000-row large CSV from the guide in a writable project.
positive: Prepare and inspect row count and preview, then accept once.
positive_expected: The count reflects all rows, preview is bounded to 100 rows / 64 KiB, and one dataset is created.
negative: Click Accept again without a new preview, then attempt preparation with no writable project.
negative_expected: Both actions are refused with an informative status and do not create another dataset.

title: Import Postman collection and environment
setup: Use postman-collection.json and postman-environment.json with a writable project.
positive: Browse each file, select its matching format, preview and publish explicitly.
positive_expected: Counts and proposed files match the fixture; synthetic secret detection is reported and project assets are published only after confirmation.
negative: Preview malformed.json as either format.
negative_expected: Validation errors appear, publish is unavailable and project files remain unchanged.

title: Import OpenAPI, HAR, cURL and detection
setup: Use openapi.json, traffic.har and request.curl.txt.
positive: Preview each file with AutoDetect and its explicit format; publish each to a fresh disposable project.
positive_expected: The format and expected request counts appear, then only the explicitly accepted assets are created.
negative: Select a mismatched explicit format or empty source.
negative_expected: An error is shown and no invalid import is published or executed.

title: Import preview freshness and file picker
setup: Use request.curl.txt and a writable project; fixture logs should be observable.
positive: Browse a file, inspect preview counts, warnings and source; cancel a subsequent file dialog.
positive_expected: The selected file populates source and preview; cancel preserves existing source; preview causes no HTTP request.
negative: Change the source after preview and try to publish without refreshing.
negative_expected: Publishing stale content is prevented or explicitly identified; no unintended asset is written.

title: GraphQL variables and syntax highlighting
setup: Start protocol_fixture.py on loopback port 5061.
positive: Enter http://127.0.0.1:5061/graphql, sample.graphql and {} variables; format and execute.
positive_expected: Query and variables remain editable with highlighting; response contains data.health = ready.
negative: Enter invalid JSON variables and invalid query syntax.
negative_expected: Diagnostics are visible; invalid input is not shown as a successful response.

title: GraphQL schema and network error
setup: Start the protocol fixture; it supports only the synthetic health query.
positive: Execute the health query, inspect response and edit query text.
positive_expected: A formatted response is displayed and editor remains responsive.
negative: Use an unavailable endpoint or a query the fixture rejects.
negative_expected: The transport or GraphQL error is visible; previous success is not attributed to the new request.

title: gRPC parse variants and transcript
setup: Use sample.proto and a disposable desktop session.
positive: Parse sample.proto; set /demo.Greeter/Greet and {"message":"hello"}; simulate the call.
positive_expected: A service/method is discovered and the simulated transcript reflects input.
negative: Use invalid proto and an unknown method or malformed payload.
negative_expected: The UI reports a parse or invocation diagnostic without claiming a real network call.

title: Streaming message types and state
setup: Start protocol_fixture.py; use ws://127.0.0.1:5061/ws and http://127.0.0.1:5061/events.
positive: Connect WebSocket, send hello, inspect echoed transcript and disconnect; connect SSE and inspect fixture-ready.
positive_expected: WebSocket send/receive and SSE event are visible, and disconnect returns to idle.
negative: Send before connecting, use a bad URL, or send on SSE.
negative_expected: The operation is rejected or reports an error without fabricating a message.

title: Mock rule specificity and logs
setup: Use a free loopback port and disposable mock server.
positive: Add GET /qa/{id} and GET /qa/fixed with distinct bodies; request /qa/fixed, then Refresh Logs and Reset State.
positive_expected: The exact rule wins and logs show the request; reset clears state.
negative: Request an unmatched path and attempt an invalid status or path.
negative_expected: No unrelated rule matches and invalid configuration is rejected or reported.

title: Mock fault mode matrix
setup: Start a mock on a free loopback port.
positive: For each fault choice None, DelayedResponse, HttpError, RateLimit, MalformedPayload and ConnectionTermination, add a distinct path and request it.
positive_expected: Each response, delay or termination matches the selected configured fault and is observable in logs.
negative: Enter a negative delay or invalid HTTP status.
negative_expected: Invalid values do not silently create a valid-looking rule or crash the UI.

title: Webhook listener prefix and restart
setup: Use the displayed local listener URL and prefix /webhooks/incoming.
positive: Start listener, send two synthetic POSTs, refresh events, stop and restart.
positive_expected: Matching events and count are visible and listener lifecycle is reflected.
negative: Send a request outside the prefix and try starting while the port is occupied.
negative_expected: Out-of-prefix traffic is not treated as a matching event and bind errors are visible.

title: Load testing model and threshold matrix
setup: Start local HTTP fixture; use small bounded values and explicit confirmation.
positive: Run closed-loop and open-loop models against /echo with permissive thresholds, then with an intentionally impossible latency threshold.
positive_expected: Each report identifies the model and metrics; the intentionally impossible threshold is reported failed.
negative: Use zero or negative VUs/duration and malformed threshold values.
negative_expected: Invalid configuration is rejected without generating load.

title: Dataset grid insert delete duplicate and fill
setup: Start with synthetic grid and record selected rows.
positive: Insert a row, edit email, duplicate it, select a column and Fill down, then delete a selected row and undo/redo.
positive_expected: Each action affects only the intended rows; duplicates receive unique IDs and undo/redo restores the appropriate state.
negative: Perform delete, duplicate or fill with no valid selection.
negative_expected: No unintended row changes and an appropriate status is shown.

title: Dataset grid clipboard input formats
setup: Use valid.csv, valid.tsv, clipboard.json and request.curl.txt.
positive: Copy each dataset content to clipboard and use Paste clipboard; inspect summary and resulting rows.
positive_expected: CSV, TSV and JSON are recognized with their rows; cURL is previewed without execution.
negative: Copy malformed.csv or malformed.json and paste.
negative_expected: Malformed data is diagnosed without silently inserting corrupted rows.

title: Grid export safety and results
setup: Create rows with =1+1, +1, -1 and @test in text cells; use a disposable destination.
positive: Export with Spreadsheet-safe export selected and inspect output as plain text; attach external-results.json content.
positive_expected: Formula-leading text is neutralized and external evidence is marked non-Wrangler.
negative: Disable safe export and inspect the same output as plain text; attach invalid or empty content.
negative_expected: Unsafe mode does not falsely claim neutralization; invalid result input is diagnosed or left unattached.

title: Git clone and remote configuration
setup: Create a disposable local bare repository as instructed in the guide.
positive: Enter its local path as remote URL and an empty destination, click Clone; add and select a second local remote.
positive_expected: Clone and remote selection are reflected in status and local Git configuration.
negative: Clone to a nonempty destination or select an unknown remote.
negative_expected: An error is displayed and existing files and remote configuration are preserved.

title: Git branch and integration operations
setup: Create disposable branches with known commits and an initial clean working tree.
positive: Create and switch branches, fast-forward, merge a non-conflicting branch and rebase a second branch.
positive_expected: History and current branch show the requested operations and preserve unrelated project files.
negative: Attempt a fast-forward of divergent history and switch with conflicting dirty changes.
negative_expected: The operation is refused or reports conflicts without silently discarding work.

title: Git restore and history
setup: Commit an editable project asset in a disposable repository, then change it.
positive: Load History, enter its repository-relative path and revision, and use Restore path.
positive_expected: History shows commits and the targeted asset returns to the selected revision.
negative: Try a nonexistent revision or a path outside api-wrangler/.
negative_expected: Restore is rejected; no outside or unrelated file is modified.

title: Git conflict resolution choices
setup: Create and reset a disposable conflict for each variant.
positive: Load versions; separately review edited result, local, incoming, deletion and save both to a valid new path; inspect each final diff and resolve.
positive_expected: Each reviewed choice produces the expected staged result and recovery copies; save both keeps both versions.
negative: Modify the draft after review or choose an existing/outside save-both path.
negative_expected: Stale review or unsafe destination is rejected and original conflict data remains recoverable.

title: GitHub compare and push failures
setup: Use a disposable repository and a synthetic GitHub remote; do not push to production.
positive: Enter a valid GitHub comparison base and branch, then click Compare.
positive_expected: A browser opens the intended comparison URL without embedding credentials.
negative: Use a non-GitHub remote or missing base and attempt Compare; push to an unreachable local remote.
negative_expected: An informative error appears and no unintended browser target or repository update occurs.

title: Shell resize, focus and read-only panels
setup: Run at 800x600 and a larger window on Windows 11 x64.
positive: Visit each top-level and nested tab, resize, drag both editor splitters, and use Tab, Shift+Tab and access keys.
positive_expected: Controls remain reachable, focus visible, splitters move and read-only output cannot be edited.
negative: Try inaccessible disabled actions with no project and inspect screen at minimum size and high contrast.
negative_expected: No crash or hidden state change occurs; clipping, missing labels or inaccessible controls are recorded as defects.
